limitations: Post hoc positions from 72 retained real-KataGo games, not fresh match outcomes.
The 12 qualification cases are included in the full corpus; qualification results are already known.
Teacher is one explicitly pinned CNN component of the four-model training mixture.
Counterfactual native pass scores are not new KataGo adjudications.
More passes may only concede known losses and do not establish stronger play.
No training, new KataGo matches, throughput/MFU claim or production promotion follows directly.
metrics: independent root policy/choice reconstruction from raw priors, visits and value sums
pass rates and paired action changes for student/teacher on/off
native terminal-pass outcomes and backup perspective
root value-range, network-value and pass-prior distributions
unscaled choice using the same recorded scaled-setting evidence
qualification_observation: All 12 original student decisions and counts reproduced; independent reconstructed policies were bit-exact. In the six after-pass cases, rescaling off changed four student actions but did not change pass count (2/6 in each setting). This does not establish that rescaling explains the refusals.
stopping_rule: One bounded attempt on four CPU worker groups. Any original-decision, native-state, backup, model-identity or independent search-reconstruction mismatch prevents interpreting the full diagnostic as qualified. Preserve all failures.
